passage:
For science week, students built solar ovens from boxes, foil, plastic wrap, and black paper. They used sunlight to warm food.
Some ovens worked better than others. Students compared angles, materials, and insulation.
The project was simple, but it taught energy transfer clearly. Sunlight could become heat if captured well.
A student from an apartment with little kitchen space asked if solar cooking was used in real places. The teacher explained that it can help where fuel is costly or sunlight is strong.
The solar oven turned a pizza box into a lesson. Science does not always need expensive equipment to reveal big ideas.
